# M22-S4: a function marked //logos:zeroalloc fails the build with
# [perf::zeroalloc_violation] when it allocates on the heap (SPEC Sec 22.4).
# The directive is the author's assertion, so no policy lowers it and no
# //logos:allow directive silences it. In a Go package only logos lint reads
# the directive.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

mkdir $WORK/bin

# A marked function that does not allocate builds and runs.
cd clean
logos build -o $WORK/bin/clean$GOEXE .
! stderr .
exec $WORK/bin/clean$GOEXE
stdout 'total=6'
cd ..

# A marked function that allocates fails the build. The diagnostic names the
# rule, the function, the allocating expression, and why escape analysis puts
# it on the heap, at the line of the allocation, and no binary is written.
cd bad
! logos build -o $WORK/bin/bad$GOEXE .
stderr 'main\.lgo:7:\d+: \[perf::zeroalloc_violation\] pack allocates: \[\]int\{\.\.\.\} escapes to heap: flows to result ~r0 \(return\)'
stderr 'main\.lgo:12:\d+: \[perf::zeroalloc_violation\] \(\*box\)\.clone allocates: &box\{\.\.\.\} escapes to heap: flows to result ~r0 \(return\)'
! stderr 'warning:'
! exists $WORK/bin/bad$GOEXE
cd ..

# The JSON record carries the rule and forbid, the severity no configuration
# lowers.
cd bad
! logos build --json-diagnostics -o $WORK/bin/bad$GOEXE .
stderr '"severity":"forbid","rule_id":"perf::zeroalloc_violation","file":"[^"]*main\.lgo","span":\{"start_line":7,'
cd ..

# perf = "allow" and a //logos:allow directive on the line change nothing.
cd policy
! logos build -o $WORK/bin/policy$GOEXE .
stderr 'main\.lgo:6:\d+: \[perf::zeroalloc_violation\] pack allocates:'
! exists $WORK/bin/policy$GOEXE
cd ..

# A directive that marks nothing fails the build: here a blank line separates
# it from the function.
cd misplaced
! logos build -o $WORK/bin/misplaced$GOEXE .
stderr 'main\.lgo:3:\d+: \[perf::zeroalloc_violation\] //logos:zeroalloc must be on its own line directly above a function declaration'
cd ..

# A Go package: logos lint reports the allocation and writes no binary;
# logos build and go build ignore the directive.
cd gopkg
! logos lint ./...
stderr 'main\.go:5:\d+: \[perf::zeroalloc_violation\] pack allocates: \[\]int\{\.\.\.\} escapes to heap: flows to result ~r0 \(return\)'
logos build ./...
! stderr .
go build ./...
! stderr .
cd ..

-- clean/go.mod --
module example.com/clean

go 1.27

-- clean/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

//logos:zeroalloc
func total(xs []int) int {
	n := 0
	for _, x := range xs {
		n += x
	}
	return n
}

func main() {
	fmt.Printf("total=%d\n", total([]int{1, 2, 3}))
}

-- bad/go.mod --
module example.com/bad

go 1.27

-- bad/main.lgo --
package main

type box struct{ v int }

//logos:zeroalloc
func pack(v int) []int {
	return []int{v}
}

//logos:zeroalloc
func (b *box) clone() *box {
	return &box{b.v}
}

func main() {
	println(len(pack(1)), (&box{1}).clone().v)
}

-- policy/go.mod --
module example.com/policy

go 1.27

-- policy/logos.toml --
[lints]
perf = "allow"

-- policy/main.lgo --
package main

//logos:zeroalloc
func pack(v int) []int {
	//logos:allow(perf::zeroalloc_violation)
	return []int{v}
}

func main() {
	println(len(pack(1)))
}

-- misplaced/go.mod --
module example.com/misplaced

go 1.27

-- misplaced/main.lgo --
package main

//logos:zeroalloc

func bump(n int) int {
	return n + 1
}

func main() {
	println(bump(1))
}

-- gopkg/go.mod --
module example.com/gopkg

go 1.27

-- gopkg/main.go --
package main

//logos:zeroalloc
func pack(v int) []int {
	return []int{v}
}

func main() {
	println(len(pack(1)))
}
